title: Social Nudity
description: Normalised nudity — at a nude beach, a naturist venue, or as a life drawing model — removes the sexual charge from being seen. What remains when arousal isn't the frame is worth knowing.
equipment: An appropriate venue: a nude beach, naturist club, clothing-optional spa, or life drawing session open to volunteer models.

instructions.label: Solo
instructions.content: Choose a context where nudity is the norm rather than the exception: a nude beach, a naturist club, a clothing-optional spa, or a life drawing session as the model. The conditions matter — you want a setting where no one is surprised or interested in the fact of your nudity, because that social neutrality is the point. Once there, resist the reflex to remain covered or mentally brace. Notice what the experience actually produces: whether the absence of erotic framing changes how you relate to your own body, whether being seen without sexual interest feels different from being seen in a charged context, and whether it's more or less comfortable than you expected. Life drawing is a particularly clean version of this — the model is closely studied and deliberately attended to, but as a subject for rendering rather than desire. That quality of being seen-but-not-desired is worth isolating as its own thing.

explore: Does being naked in a non-sexual context feel liberating, exposing, neutral — or something harder to name?
Is there more self-consciousness when being seen without sexual framing, or less?
Does the absence of erotic charge change how you relate to your own body in the moment — does the body feel different when it isn't performing anything?
If you've tried exhibitionism, how does removing the erotic charge change the experience — is the difference between contexts significant, or is being seen simply being seen?
why: Social nudity isolates a variable that exhibitionism mixes in: being seen without any erotic charge in either direction. Naturist contexts deliberately defuse the sexual register — the social contract is that nudity is not an invitation, not a display, and not particularly significant. For some people, that neutrality is a relief: the body exists without performing anything, and there's nothing to manage in others' responses. For others, the absence of sexual framing makes the experience feel flat, which is itself informative — it suggests the charge in exhibitionist contexts comes specifically from the erotic attention rather than from being seen in general. Life drawing adds a further layer: the model's body is actively attended to and studied, which is a form of close looking that has no erotic content but isn't indifferent either.
